In mathematics, the '''Dwork unit root zeta function''', named after [[Bernard Dwork]], is the [[L-function]] attached to the [[p-adic]] [[Galois representation]] arising from the p-adic [[etale cohomology]] of an [[algebraic variety]] defined over a [[global function field]] of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]]&nbsp;''p''.  The '''Dwork conjecture''' (1973) states that his unit root zeta function is p-adic [[meromorphic function|meromorphic]] everywhere.<ref>{{citation|last=Dwork|first=Bernard|authorlink=Bernard Dwork|title=Normalized period matrices II|year=1973|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=98|issue=1|pages=1–57|doi=10.2307/1970905|jstor=1970905 }}.</ref> This conjecture was proved 
by [[Daqing Wan|Wan]] (2000).<ref>{{citation|last=Wan|first=Daqing|title=Dwork's conjecture on unit root zeta functions|year=1999|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=150|issue=3|pages=867–927|arxiv=math/9911270|doi=10.2307/121058|jstor=121058 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Wan|first=Daqing|title=Higher rank case of Dwork's conjecture|year=2000|journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=13|issue=4|pages=807–852|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00339-8|doi-access=free}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Wan|first=Daqing|title=Rank one case of Dwork's conjecture|year=2000|journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=13|issue=4|pages=853–908|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00340-4|doi-access=free}}.</ref>
